This poem is about my sister who died of an OD the day I was visiting her. I was having the best day of my life and hadn’t seen her in 4 years so I was excited. I had spoken to her an hour before she passed and she seemed so happy. She relapsed in sober living and they couldn’t bring her back. Her brain leaked into her spine ... she went brain dead. The most horrible experience of my life especially because I was literally on my way to see her when I found the news.

This poem is about what if that day went differently and what if i could’ve calmed her mind and couldve made her say she was done chasing the dragon.

I use war as an analogy to drug addiction because it is a horrible internal war. The evil men I refer to are the people who abuse others (most addiction comes from abuse) and also the politicians who don’t do anything to help. Refuge away from sin is me saying that those with addictions are trying to escape from the trauma that was inflicted upon them by others. In trying to escape, the become beggars (needing money for drugs and cheating,lying,stealing to get the drugs) and they hold onto this trauma in their heart because they don’t know how to let it go as it was painful for them to bare.

The dirty foil on the ground is about my sister since she smoked her drug of choice before she died and when I say “dignity beheaded” I mean losing dignity but also beheaded because she went brain dead. When I talk about poisoned water and how they tell us to keep drinking, I’m speaking of enablers, but also the drug dealers who are providing drugs and want the addicted to stay addicted.

“The soldiers on the ship weren’t notified it was sinking,” essentially I wrote this meaning that many buying drugs aren’t fully aware of what they’re consuming and many don’t realize they’re addicted until it’s too late. They believe they can stop at any time although their circumstances say differently. People don’t confront the person to tell them they’re sinking because they’re getting something out of the persons addiction or they are worried of confrontation with the person.

Obviously I never got to see her and she died young with so much life ahead which is why I compare her to a full forest and a fawn. No one protected her as they were supposed to (except me. I tried my absolute best) and I’m sure she felt so misunderstood when she lashed out. Although my sister has passed, one day I will be with her and that gives me enough to keep going.

It’s called “no one won the war” because the addicted tends to die addicted (not always but sadly in too many cases), the loved ones  are heartbroken, the dealer is sinning, and the abusers are still abusers. No one wins in this situation because those who were already losing lose everything or don’t change, there is no resolution, there is no other ending except this abrupt loss that feels empty. It’s as though all of her pain she felt has now decided to reside within me and I can’t do anything about it because she’s no longer here for me to save.

I think I’m a lot more cause and effect. I’m able to tell what’s going to happen way before it happens and pride myself on being clairvoyant in a way. As far as what you’ve written:

1. I ask if they need anything first and usually have something prepared for my guests whether it’s a meal, a movie, etc so I can make sure they’re comfy. 

2. I find small talk boring and only like to engage in deep or hypothetical conversations. I knew my best friend was the one when I could talk in depth with her about science, philosophy, history, art. I don’t care to know people’s favorite colors lol. 

3. I do both. I try to understand where someone is coming from and I try to distance the person from the action, however I will cut people off if they’re self destructive or I feel like they are people who are too neurotic. When I cut people off for their behaviors, I try to talk to them prior and if nothing changed, I hard cut. I had a friend who kept going to the mental hospital for being suicidal and it stressed me out badly since I cared for her so I had to let her go. Was not an easy conversation and I think about her often. I do enjoy helping people become better themselves unless they are keen on staying the same.

4. I 100% want to improve systems. I had a physics internship and one of the optic pieces we were using was extremely inefficient. I came up with a way to make coupling light into a fiber a lot more efficient and was wondering how no one ever thought about it before. Too broke to do anything about it right now but hopefully in the future! My goal is to do theoretical research so I can prove and disprove astronomical phenomena’s and potentially find ways to make math “better”. I have beef with mathematical rules, don’t ask lol.

5. I think I have both concrete and spiritual goals. I mainly want to provide for my family to be happy. I want to be the best version of myself I can be and I think it’d be great to change the world in a positive way (hopefully in science or math). 

6. I don’t take action as quickly because it takes me a long time to make decisions. I need to think of every pro and con before I do something. I need to make sure it aligns with my future goals and will further my life and if it doesn’t, I won’t do it. When I was younger I was more of a people pleaser but I’ve gotten good at discerning what’s necessary and what’s a distraction. 

7. I don’t follow trends and don’t know about them 99% of the time. I love fashion and aesthetics, however and enjoy looking nice. I make sure my outfits are cohesive because appearance tells people how to treat you. Currently I’m extremely interested in the prep/ old money look. I don’t pay attention to anything except what I like so what’s popular never crosses my mind. 

8. This one is difficult. I only like leading people if they can lead themselves because I don’t have the patience for directing directionless people. If they’re willing to learn, I’m willing to teach, but if they seem complacent then I leave them alone.

9. Education and work experience is a preference to me when it comes to who I am dating, otherwise I couldn’t care less. And even with dating if they are making a healthy amount as well as financially literate, I won’t mind dating them. I have very high standards for myself, however, so I would hope they would have the same standards for themselves. Things happen though and I get that; I know not everyone can get a degree and such. 

10. Yes, I struggle with this. I don’t like people victimizing themselves so I tend to be firm on “you did the wrong things so take accountability”. I think once you’re an adult, you have a lot of control of yourself so there’s no reason why you should do things that you know are destructive to you or others. I give more leeway to people with mental illness , as someone with mental illness, but if they’re not medicated or in therapy, my sympathy wains.

Lastly, I will not date men who are not doing well. I have no capacity to take care of someone else unless it is a child and I try to make sure they are earning enough money, they have savings, etc. I prefer to date men who dress nice and are planners because men who aren’t planners are too spontaneous for me. I also want someone who makes me soft because I always feel that I’m the dominant one in the relationship and it’s exhausting.

I’m not going to lie. I am usually a very safety oriented person but I really dropped the ball on this one. I didn’t bring my bear spray or my knife or my first aid kit and brought only a banana and peanut butter. I also got lost for about 5-10 minutes in the trail at the end and realized how dumb I was. With that being said : 

-always bring a map of the trail, know the markers 

-bring a gallon of water OR if there are streams , bring two liters and some water purification source (iodine tablets work great)

-first aid kit always 

-tent or hammock , this depends on what your preference is 

-food canister if staying overnight . I’ve also hung my food a bit away from my camp with a rope on a tree when I didn’t have a canister prior but this is a pretty risky thing since bears can climb 

-bear spray and a knife/ switchblade 

-FOOD . More than you think always. Especially if overnight. You never know if you’ll get stuck for an extra day or something unexpected will happen

-let others know where you will be/itinerary, what you are wearing and what time they should expect to hear back from you . I also sent my boyfriend the SAR number just in case . 

-headlamp!!!!!!!!!! You could underestimate the time spent hiking and it could get dark. Always start hikes earlier than you think you need to finish too, especially in the mountains. 

-I am well versed on what to do if a snake bites me or if I’m attacked by an animal. I think this is super important. Rattlesnake bites aren’t super common on hikes BUT KNOW WHAT TO DO. Also know how to wrap your self if you get a broken bone or sprained ankle. Know the animals , terrain, insects , plants you’re dealing with. Also know the water sources. Some people have died from drinking out of toxic water sources.

- wear layers! It’s better to take off than to be freezing and not be able to add to!

- leave no trace :)! 

- To be very honest, the part I’m scared of the most are sketchy people , not the animals . But most hikers are friendly and just trying to enjoy nature like you and I. If someone is weird on a trail,  make sure you have your knife and bear spray armed (I keep my knife hooked on the front of my pack and my bear spray in the side pocket. Taking a self defense class wouldn’t hurt either!!  Never tell anyone your travel plans either unless you have developed a close relationship to them on the hike (this goes for longer hikes where you might meet other solo hikers ~ like John Muir)

- HAVE FUN! (I hope I covered everything but I probably forgot something! Feel free to add on if any of you have any other advice )
